Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Other Sports FIP Bronze S2 Accra: Ghana takes major step in Padel development with historic tournament Source : Adamu Benin Abdul Karim 22 November 2026 11:45pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghana made history on Sunday as the first International Padel Federation Bronze tournament in the country successfully concluded at the S2 Sport Club in Spintex, Accra.
The FIP Bronze S2 Accra, which offered world ranking points and entry into the professional circuit, ran for a week and crowned champions in both the men’s and women’s categories.
Spain’s Adrian Lopez and Guillem Santiago claimed the men’s title after beating Egypt’s George Wakim and Morocco’s Mohamed Alami in straight sets.
The Spanish pair won 6-4, 6-1 following a tougher semi-final earlier in the day.
Santiago says he is already looking forward to returning to Ghana for the next edition.
“Great tournament. Great crowd. Great organisation. It’s our first time here, and we enjoyed it a lot. I hope we will come back next year.”
In the women’s category, Spain’s Cayetana Sanchez Vera and Greece’s Christina Ntanou also won the title with a straight-sets victory over France’s Cimille Siriex and the Netherlands’ Tess de Vocht.
They won 6-3, 6-4 after cruising to a 6-1, 6-1 semi-final victory.
The victory also marked a personal milestone for Vera and Ntanou, who claimed their first international medals in Ghana.
For Professional Padel Association of Ghana president Jean Noel Said, the tournament has already made a significant impact on the growth of the sport in the country.
“It means improvement, growth and development because we started padel in Ghana four years ago, and today we're hosting the first FIP Bronze tournament in the country. I think it shows that the community is growing and that there's an interest in the sport in Ghana.
“We want to give the youth an opportunity to see what the pros are doing, how they're performing and how they're playing. I think it's a great opportunity for them. The kids really enjoyed it. They were interacting with the pros, asking questions and playing with them, so I think it was a great move.”
His vice-president, Nour Seklaoui, added: “Two years ago, when the federation was formed, nobody thought we would get here that quickly. Part of our mission and vision was to achieve this, and we can see now that the sky is the limit. If we're able to host an FIP Bronze tournament in just two years, you never know when we will host Silver and then Gold tournaments. This is a great achievement for Ghana.”
The tournament ended on a celebratory note, with the medal ceremony turning into a birthday celebration for Said and Moroccan player Mohamed Alami.
